articles.title: Thuthukile Zuma Resigns from ANC Greater Joburg REC Amid Accountability Questions
articles.summary: The ANC Greater Johannesburg Region had reportedly requested that Zuma account for her alleged failure to discharge her duties as an REC member, as well as questions surrounding her participation in the ANC's campaign activities during the 2026 Local Government Elections.
articles.body:
Johannesburg – Thuthukile Zuma, popularly known as Thuthu, has reportedly resigned from the African National Congress (ANC) Greater Johannesburg Regional Executive Committee (REC), following questions raised by the regional leadership regarding her conduct, participation and fulfilment of responsibilities as a member of the regional structure.

According to sources familiar with the developments, the ANC Greater Johannesburg Region had reportedly requested that Zuma account for her alleged failure to discharge her duties as an REC member, as well as questions surrounding her participation in the ANC's campaign activities during the 2026 Local Government Elections.

Sources indicate that Zuma was afforded an opportunity to respond to the allegations levelled against her, with the deadline reportedly extended to 20 November 2026. However, rather than proceeding with the accountability process, she allegedly opted to tender her resignation.

It is understood that, in communicating her decision, Zuma reportedly raised concerns about what she perceived as mistreatment by members of the REC, suggesting that her resignation was informed, at least in part, by her experience within the regional leadership structure.

The concerns reportedly extend to her attendance record, with sources claiming that the ANC has documentation reflecting several instances of absenteeism from compulsory REC meetings. These meetings are considered important platforms for organisational coordination, political accountability and the implementation of regional programmes.

Social media exchange raises further questions

The matter has also reportedly attracted attention following an alleged exchange between Zuma and ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula on the social media platform X.

According to sources, her conduct on the platform forms part of broader concerns about organisational discipline and what has been characterised as behaviour inconsistent with the traditions and protocols of the ANC.

It is alleged that Zuma was expected to account for what some within the organisation regarded as conduct unbecoming of an ANC leader, particularly given the established internal mechanisms available to members for raising grievances, disagreements and organisational concerns.

The ANC's organisational culture places emphasis on internal consultation, discipline and established channels of communication when dealing with differences within its structures.

Resignation amid unanswered questions

Her reported resignation comes at a time when the ANC is intensifying its organisational preparations and campaign activities ahead of the 2026 Local Government Elections.

The development raises questions about the relationship between Zuma and the regional leadership, particularly whether the disagreements surrounding her alleged treatment within the REC contributed to her decision to step down.

It also remains unclear whether the regional leadership will continue pursuing the outstanding accountability matters following her reported resignation.

At the time of publication, Thuthukile Zuma had not responded to the allegations or publicly provided her version of events. The ANC Greater Johannesburg Region had also issued an official statement confirming the circumstances surrounding her reported departure.

This publication will provide Zuma and the ANC Greater Johannesburg Region an opportunity to respond should they wish to clarify the matter.
articles.author: Kabelo Zwelibuyile Hlongwane
